steps.intent: China's objective is to address the severe security, economic, and environmental ramifications of the Nord Stream sabotage by establishing an authoritative, transparent, and impartial UN-led international commission of inquiry. The most difficult negotiating point will be overcoming the resistance of Western Council members, who maintain that ongoing national investigations by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden must run their course without UN intervention and who view the initiative as politicized. Achieving the required nine affirmative votes without provoking Western abstentions or vetoes will require emphasizing depoliticized technical cooperation and the protection of global transnational infrastructure.

messages.Albania: Albania sees no added value in establishing a UN commission of inquiry when competent, independent national investigations by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden are already underway. We have full confidence in these national authorities and believe creating a parallel mechanism would merely duplicate efforts and politicize the matter. Unless the text refrains from undermining ongoing national proceedings, Albania will not be in a position to support it.
messages.Brazil: Brazil considers the sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines a matter of grave concern that threatens critical infrastructure, maritime safety, and environmental security. We support the establishment of an independent, impartial, and objective UN investigation to establish the facts and ensure accountability. To build broader Council consensus, we suggest clarifying that the proposed international commission would work in complementarity with, rather than duplicate or undermine, ongoing national investigations.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador condemns all attacks against critical civilian infrastructure and expresses serious concern regarding the environmental and economic ramifications of the Nord Stream sabotage. Nevertheless, independent and professional national investigations are currently being conducted by the relevant coastal and affected States. The Security Council must respect these ongoing national judicial processes and avoid duplicating efforts or establishing a parallel mechanism prematurely.
messages.France: France strongly condemns the acts of sabotage against the Nord Stream pipelines, which represent a serious incident for European energy security and the environment. However, thorough, independent, and professional criminal investigations are already being actively carried out by the competent authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. France sees no added value or justification for establishing an international commission of inquiry at this stage, which risks politicizing the issue and interfering with ongoing judicial proceedings.
messages.Gabon: Gabon condemns all acts of sabotage against critical civilian and transnational infrastructure, which have serious environmental and economic repercussions. However, credible national investigations by the relevant coastal States are already underway, and we believe they must be given the time and space to run their course before establishing an international mechanism. We urge the Council to seek consensus and avoid initiatives that divide the membership while these national processes remain active.
messages.Ghana: Ghana views any deliberate attack on critical undersea infrastructure as a grave threat to international peace, security, and the marine environment that warrants full accountability. However, credible national investigations by competent authorities in Denmark, Germany, and Sweden are already underway, and they should be allowed to run their course rather than establishing a parallel UN mechanism that lacks Council consensus. Unless the draft gives precedence to concluding these ongoing domestic investigations, Ghana will be constrained to abstain on this text.
messages.Japan: Japan condemns all acts of sabotage against critical civilian and transnational infrastructure. However, credible, transparent, and thorough investigations are already actively underway by the competent authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Creating a parallel UN commission of inquiry would unnecessarily duplicate efforts and undermine these legitimate ongoing national processes, which must be allowed to conclude without politicization.
messages.Malta: Malta unequivocally condemns the sabotage against the Nord Stream pipelines and recognizes the serious energy, maritime, and environmental concerns stemming from these incidents. However, rigorous and independent national investigations are actively being conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Establishing a parallel UN investigation at this stage would duplicate ongoing efforts and question the integrity of competent national authorities, which Malta cannot support.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique is deeply concerned by the attacks against critical cross-border energy infrastructure and agrees that those responsible must be held accountable. However, thorough national investigations by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden are currently underway and should be allowed to run their course. Without broad consensus and given the risk of duplicating existing investigative processes, Mozambique cannot support the immediate establishment of a separate UN mechanism and will be inclined to abstain.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation fully supports the draft resolution, which addresses a critical threat to international peace, security, and global energy infrastructure resulting from the unprecedented sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines. The ongoing national investigations conducted by certain European states are utterly non-transparent, protracted, and deliberately exclude Russia as the affected state and infrastructure owner. An independent, objective, and comprehensive international investigation established under the auspices of the United Nations Secretary-General is imperative to uncover the truth and hold the perpetrators, sponsors, and organizers accountable.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland condemns all attacks against critical infrastructure and underscores the importance of accountability for the Nord Stream sabotage. However, independent and professional national investigations are already actively underway by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. The Security Council should avoid duplicating efforts or undermining these competent processes and instead await their conclusions before considering any international investigative mechanism.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates unequivocally condemns attacks on critical transnational energy infrastructure and supports efforts to ensure accountability. However, the Security Council should avoid duplicating efforts while thorough national investigations by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden are actively underway. Establishing a new UN investigative mechanism requires broad agreement and consensus among Council members, which is currently lacking.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support the creation of a United Nations commission of inquiry while rigorous, independent, and professional national investigations are already well underway by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Establishing a parallel UN investigation would duplicate efforts, expend unnecessary resources, and serve only to politicize this issue. Council members should allow the competent authorities of the coastal States to conclude their work without external interference.
messages.United States of America: The United States firmly condemns the sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines, but there is no need or justification for establishing a duplicate UN commission of inquiry. Thorough, professional, and independent national investigations by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden are actively under way, and the Council must allow these competent authorities to conclude their work without political interference. This draft resolution is clearly intended to discredit and prejudge those ongoing inquiries, and the United States cannot support it.

messages.Albania: Albania maintains full confidence in the rigorous, independent, and professional national investigations currently being conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Establishing a parallel United Nations commission of inquiry is completely unnecessary, risks politicizing the process, and duplicates ongoing legal efforts. Without the removal of operative paragraph 2, Albania cannot support this draft resolution and will abstain.
messages.Brazil: Brazil thanks the penholders for positively considering and incorporating our proposals regarding complementarity and coordination with ongoing national investigations. We consider the sabotage of critical transnational infrastructure a grave matter with far-reaching economic and environmental implications that merits an impartial, transparent, and credible international inquiry. With the text appropriately reflecting the need to respect and build upon existing national efforts, Brazil is in a position to support the draft resolution as presented.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador reiterates that the Security Council should respect and avoid duplicating the thorough, ongoing investigations currently being conducted by the competent national authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Establishing a parallel United Nations commission of inquiry at this stage is premature and undermines confidence in national judicial processes. Unless our core concern regarding OP2 is addressed to allow national investigations to conclude first, Ecuador will not be in a position to support this draft resolution and will abstain.
messages.France: France reiterates its full confidence in the independent, professional, and transparent investigations currently being conducted by the competent national authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Establishing a parallel United Nations commission of inquiry would duplicate ongoing efforts, undermine national judicial proceedings, and politicize the matter. Since the text continues to establish such an unnecessary mechanism, France cannot support this draft resolution and will abstain if it is put to a vote.
messages.Gabon: Gabon notes the penholder's efforts to acknowledge national investigations in the preamble, but our primary concern regarding the immediate establishment of an international commission of inquiry remains unresolved. We believe that national investigations currently conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden must be allowed to conclude their work without preemption or unnecessary duplication. In the absence of modification to operative paragraph 2 to respect the primacy of these ongoing proceedings, Gabon will be unable to support the draft resolution and will abstain.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the penholder's inclusion of references to Denmark, Germany, and Sweden in PP6. However, our delegation firmly believes that the ongoing national investigations should be allowed to run their course and report their findings before the Council considers creating an international commission of inquiry. Without deferring the establishment of a UN-mandated mechanism to avoid duplication and prejudgment, Ghana cannot support the text and will be obliged to abstain.
messages.Japan: Japan reiterates that rigorous, independent, and professional national investigations are currently being conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden in accordance with the rule of law. Establishing a separate United Nations commission of inquiry at this stage is duplicative and undermines the credibility of these competent national authorities. As long as the draft insists on establishing a new investigative mechanism rather than awaiting the findings of the ongoing investigations, Japan cannot support it and will abstain.
messages.Malta: Malta reiterates its full trust and confidence in the ongoing, independent national investigations currently being conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Establishing a parallel United Nations investigative mechanism at this juncture is unjustified, duplicates efforts, and risks politicizing the process before national authorities have concluded their work. As our core concerns regarding the necessity of a UN commission of inquiry have not been addressed, Malta cannot support the draft resolution in its current form and will abstain if it is put to a vote.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique appreciates the penholder's accommodation of language on coordination and complementarity. However, our principled view remains that the ongoing national investigations by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden should be allowed to conclude before the Council establishes an independent international mechanism. In the absence of consensus and given the risk of prejudicing or duplicating ongoing domestic inquiries, Mozambique intends to abstain on the draft in its current form.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation fully supports the revised draft resolution and commends China for its balanced and principled leadership as penholder. The text establishes an essential, objective, and transparent UN mechanism to investigate this unprecedented act of international terrorism against critical transnational infrastructure. We urge all Council members to support this draft and look forward to putting it to an immediate vote.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland reiterates that attacks against critical infrastructure are unacceptable, but full confidence must be placed in the rigorous, independent national investigations currently being conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden under the rule of law. Establishing a parallel United Nations commission of inquiry at this stage risks duplicating efforts and interfering with ongoing judicial proceedings. If the text continues to establish a UN investigation rather than allowing national authorities to complete their work, Switzerland will abstain.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates underscores the critical importance of safeguarding transnational energy infrastructure and ensuring accountability for acts of sabotage. However, establishing a new United Nations investigative mechanism requires broad consensus among Council members, which is clearly lacking at this stage. Given that rigorous national investigations by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden are ongoing and should be allowed to run their course, the UAE cannot support the establishment of a parallel commission of inquiry and will abstain if the draft remains unchanged.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom reiterates that there is no justification or legal basis for establishing a United Nations commission of inquiry while rigorous, independent, and impartial national investigations are actively being conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Mandating an unnecessary parallel UN mechanism seeks only to politicize this issue and undermine these established, professional national processes. Unless the text is fundamentally revised to remove the mandate for a UN investigation and fully respect the ongoing national efforts, the United Kingdom cannot support this draft.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft resolution, which is entirely unnecessary and transparently designed to undermine and politicize the credible, independent, and rigorous national investigations currently being conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Establishing a duplicate UN commission of inquiry would serve only to distract from the facts and waste Council resources. Unless the mechanism establishing an international investigation is removed, the United States will not support this text.

before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

Today, the Security Council has an opportunity to take a principled and necessary decision to establish the truth regarding an unprecedented act of international terrorism: the sabotage of the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 gas pipelines in September 2022. 

The destruction of this critical transnational energy infrastructure has had grave repercussions for international peace and security, energy security, and the marine environment. More than six months have passed since this attack, yet the so-called national investigations conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden remain entirely opaque to the international community and to the affected States, including the Russian Federation, which has been systematically denied access to information and participation. 

The draft resolution before us today, prepared in close cooperation with our Chinese colleagues and co-sponsored by a wide circle of States, is balanced, depoliticized, and purely objective. It requests the Secretary-General to establish an independent, impartial international commission of inquiry to establish all the circumstances of the sabotage, identify perpetrators, sponsors, and accomplices, and complement existing efforts. 

Those who have nothing to hide should have no reason to fear an impartial and transparent international investigation under the auspices of the United Nations. A vote in favour of this draft resolution is a vote for accountability, transparency, and the rule of international law. We urge all Council members to support this text.

after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil voted in favour of the draft resolution presented today. 

Brazil condemns in the strongest terms any acts of sabotage against critical civilian and transnational energy infrastructure, including the attacks perpetrated against the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 pipelines in September 2022. Such acts have severe repercussions not only for international peace and security and energy stability, but also for the global marine environment. 

Given the gravity and unprecedented nature of this incident, Brazil considers that a comprehensive, transparent, impartial, and independent investigation under the auspices of the United Nations would be appropriate to establish the facts, identify those responsible, and hold them accountable. 

Our vote in favour was guided by the conviction that an international investigation led by the United Nations would not undermine or replace the national investigations currently being conducted by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden, but rather coordinate with and complement those efforts. Bringing the authority and objectivity of the United Nations to bear on this issue could help dispel doubts, enhance transparency, and foster greater confidence in the findings among the international community.

At a time of heightened geopolitical tensions, establishing the truth through an impartial and credible process is essential to de-escalate rhetoric and ensure that attacks against critical international infrastructure do not become a dangerous precedent.

Thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution just put to the vote, and we regret the outcome of the voting.

The Nord Stream gas pipelines are major transnational infrastructure facilities and energy transportation arteries. The physical destruction of the pipelines in September last year was a major incident that severely impacted global energy security, the marine environment, and international peace and security. Since the incident occurred, the international community, including many members of the Security Council, has called for a comprehensive, objective, impartial, and professional investigation to establish the truth, identify the perpetrators, and bring them to justice.

China supports the Security Council in authorizing an independent international investigation into the Nord Stream sabotage under the auspices of the United Nations. An independent international commission of inquiry, mandated by the Council and led by the Secretary-General, would play an indispensable role in ensuring transparency, objectivity, and credibility, while establishing the facts in a way that can gain the broad trust and acceptance of the international community. 

Such a UN-led international investigation would not stand in opposition to the ongoing national investigations conducted by the countries concerned. Rather, as clearly stated in the draft resolution, it would coordinate with and complement national efforts, helping to ensure the integrity of the findings and preventing any suspicion of concealment or double standards. 

Although the draft resolution was not adopted today, the call of the international community for truth and accountability will not cease. National investigations by Sweden, Denmark, and Germany have been underway for more than six months, yet the international community has received very little information regarding their progress and findings. We hope that the countries concerned will accelerate their investigations, maintain timely and effective communication with affected parties and the Security Council, and release the results of their investigations without delay. On matters concerning critical international infrastructure, the international community is entitled to the full truth.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Ecuador:
Mr. President,

Ecuador abstained in the voting on the draft resolution presented today.

Ecuador condemns any act of sabotage or attack against critical civilian infrastructure, including transnational energy infrastructure. Such acts not only pose risks to international peace and security and energy security, but also have grave environmental consequences, particularly for the marine environment.

We emphasize that it is essential to establish the truth of the events of September 2022 regarding the Nord Stream pipelines, identify those responsible, and ensure full accountability.

However, competent national authorities in Denmark, Germany, and Sweden are currently conducting comprehensive, rigorous, and independent investigations into these incidents in accordance with their national legal frameworks. We believe that the Security Council and the international community should allow these national investigations to conclude and present their findings. 

Establishing a parallel international investigation under the auspices of the United Nations at this stage would not provide added value and could interfere with or duplicate the ongoing work of national authorities. For these reasons, Ecuador decided to abstain on the draft resolution.

I thank you.
after.France:
(spoke in French):

France abstained on the draft resolution submitted to the Council today.

France has clearly condemned the acts of sabotage committed in September 2022 against the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 gas pipelines in the Baltic Sea, which damaged critical infrastructure and had serious consequences for the environment. 

However, independent, thorough, and professional national investigations are currently being conducted by the competent authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden, in full compliance with their national legislation and international legal standards. France has complete confidence in the integrity, impartiality, and professionalism of the judicial and investigative authorities of these three democratic States. 

There was therefore no justification for establishing a parallel United Nations mechanism, which would only duplicate ongoing efforts and undermine the national investigations. It is essential to let these investigations run their course and conclude their work.

Finally, France regrets that the Russian Federation continues to instrumentalize the Security Council and consume its time and resources in an effort to divert the attention of the international community from its unlawful war of aggression against Ukraine, which constitutes a blatant violation of the United Nations Charter.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted to abstain on the draft resolution just put to the vote.

Japan condemns in the strongest terms any attacks on critical infrastructure, including underwater energy infrastructure. Such acts pose serious risks to international peace and security, energy security, and the marine environment, and the perpetrators must be held accountable.

At the same time, rigorous, independent, and transparent national investigations into the sabotage of the Nord Stream pipelines are currently being carried out by the relevant authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. Japan has full confidence in the competence and integrity of these national investigations, which are being conducted in accordance with their domestic legal frameworks and international law.

We believe that there is no justifiable reason to establish a separate international investigative mechanism that would duplicate or interfere with these ongoing national efforts. It is essential that we allow these credible investigations to run their course and await their findings before contemplating any further action by the Council.

It was for these reasons that Japan abstained on the draft resolution.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland abstained in the vote on the draft resolution submitted today. 

Switzerland condemns all attacks against critical infrastructure, including energy infrastructure. The sabotage of the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 gas pipelines has had severe environmental consequences and significant implications for energy security. 

However, Switzerland has full confidence in the ongoing national investigations being conducted by the competent authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. These investigations are being carried out independently, thoroughly, and in full compliance with the rule of law. 

At this stage, while these independent national investigations are actively underway, we see no added value in establishing an international investigative mechanism under the auspices of the United Nations. We should instead allow the competent national authorities to conclude their work and await the results of these investigations before considering any further steps. 

I thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom abstained on the draft resolution before us today.

Our position on this matter has been clear and consistent. The United Kingdom condemns acts of sabotage against civilian infrastructure, including the Nord Stream pipelines. However, as Council members are well aware, competent authorities in Denmark, Germany, and Sweden are currently conducting full, impartial, and professional investigations into the incidents. 

These investigations are being carried out in accordance with domestic law and standard international procedures. The authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden have kept the Security Council informed of their progress, most recently in their joint letter to Council members in February. We have full confidence in the integrity, independence, and technical expertise of these national investigations.

There is no reason to duplicate these ongoing efforts or to spend United Nations resources on establishing a parallel mechanism when credible, independent processes are already underway. Council members should allow these national investigations to run their course and conclude their work.

It is difficult to escape the conclusion that Russia’s motivation in bringing this resolution forward was not an objective search for truth, but rather an attempt to politicize the issue and distract attention from its ongoing, unprovoked, and illegal full-scale invasion of Ukraine. 

For these reasons, the United Kingdom could not support the draft resolution and chose to abstain.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United States abstained on the draft resolution before us today.

First and foremost, let me reiterate unequivocally that the United States was not involved in any way in the acts of sabotage on the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 pipelines. Accusations to the contrary made by the Russian Federation are completely false and baseless disinformation.

The United States supports establishing the facts surrounding the damage to the Nord Stream pipelines. However, there is simply no need for an international investigation led by the United Nations when comprehensive, impartial, and transparent national investigations are already actively underway by Denmark, Germany, and Sweden. 

These three states have sophisticated, highly competent legal systems, professional investigative bodies, and marine expertise. They have been conducting rigorous technical and forensic investigations in accordance with their national legislation and international legal standards. They have also kept the Security Council regularly informed of their progress, including through their joint letter to Council members. We have full confidence in their ability to conduct thorough, independent, and credible inquiries.

Russia’s draft resolution was never about finding the truth. It was a transparent attempt to discredit and undermine the ongoing national investigations, to sow doubt and division, and to politicize an issue for its own propaganda purposes. It was an effort to deflect international attention away from Russia’s ongoing, unprovoked, and full-scale war of aggression against Ukraine, its daily war crimes, and its reckless nuclear rhetoric.

Establishing a parallel UN commission of inquiry would have unnecessarily politicized this matter, wasted precious UN resources, and interfered with ongoing domestic legal processes. For these reasons, the vast majority of Council members chose not to support this resolution.

We urge all Council members to let the competent national authorities of Denmark, Germany, and Sweden conclude their work, rather than attempting to prejudge or distract from their investigations. 

Thank you, Mr. President.
